questions.question: If a tire fails while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as possible.
Release the steering wheel.
Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Stop on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the steering wheel firmly. Do not brake. Let the vehicle slow down by itself. Once it slows down enough, brake gently, move to the side of the road, and stop.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Prevent wheels from locking up
Alert other drivers when you are braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery roads.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Change quickly before other vehicles enter the lane.
Change slowly in case another vehicle is already in that lane.
Do not use your turn signal.
Never use the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change slowly in case another vehicle is already in that lane.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives drivers you did not see time to move out of your way or honk to warn you. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.
The front lights will flash.
The vehicle should stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on.
questions.explanation: If air pressure drops below 60 psi, a warning light or alarm will activate in an air brake system.

questions.question: A bus driver does not need to stop at a:

options.text: Raised drawbridge
Streetcar crossing
Railroad crossing
Stop sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Streetcar crossing
questions.explanation: You must stop 15 to 50 feet from railroad tracks to look and listen for trains before proceeding. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, at traffic signals showing green, if a police officer is directing traffic, or at crossings marked as exempt or abandoned.

questions.question: When should placards be used on a vehicle?

options.text: Any time the vehicle carries hazardous materials
If there is empty space in the truck
If hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds
If the materials can be inhaled

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time the vehicle carries hazardous materials
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of material is being carried and warn others of dangers.

questions.question: When inspecting the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Loosen every seat
Check every handhold
Assume all buzzers work properly
Remove the emergency exit handles

questions.correctAnswerText: Check every handhold
questions.explanation: When inspecting a bus interior, make sure everything is safe and works properly. Check that every handhold and railing is secure and safe to use.

questions.question: How much water is needed for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: Usually several inches
A large amount, like a big puddle
A small amount
None

questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on wet roads and slide on water. It does not require a large amount of water.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver has a crash ahead of you, what should you do?

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle
Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive behavior
Keep driving and do not get involved
Pull over and yell at the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive behavior
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them what you saw about the aggressive behavior.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: Retracted
Fully raised
More worn on one side than the other
Well lit

questions.correctAnswerText: Fully raised
questions.explanation: When inspecting a trailer, make sure the landing gear has all its parts and is fully raised. The crank handle should be secure and the support frame should not be damaged.

questions.question: When should you adjust mirrors?

options.text: While the vehicle is moving.
When the trailer is straight.
When you are standing next to the vehicle.
By an assistant.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start driving. If your vehicle has a trailer, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: You can drive faster than a train to cross safely.
Do not depend only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not depend only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never trust only warning signals at railroad crossings. Never try to race a train. If there are multiple tracks, check all of them in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: In an emergency while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop immediately.
Stopping is not always the safest choice.
Never swerve to avoid danger.
Always turn on your flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping is not always the safest choice.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest option in an emergency. Steering out of the way is usually safer than stopping.

questions.question: What is a sign of a distracted driver?

options.text: They stay in their lane.
They drive at a steady speed.
They are focused on their cell phone.
They are not talking to anyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are focused on their cell phone.
questions.explanation: You can tell a driver is distracted if they drift between lanes, change speeds often, focus on a cell phone, look at a map or food, or talk with passengers.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: It drains water and oil from the air tanks.
It stops air from leaking if the compressor breaks.
It activates emergency brakes when there is a leak.
It holds spring brakes in place until they are needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops air from leaking if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main air tank. It prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to get there sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.
Take an energy pill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, stop and sleep. Fighting tiredness is dangerous and causes crashes. Energy pills may keep you awake but will not make you more alert. When they wear off, you will be even more tired.

questions.question: If you are unsure your vehicle fits under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Swerve while passing under the bridge.
Slow down.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down and find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Downshift.
Pump the brakes.
Speed up.
Use the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find an escape route like an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: Where should a helper stand when backing up a vehicle?

options.text: In front of the passenger side.
In front of the driver side.
On the side of the truck.
Near the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck.
questions.explanation: Your helper should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Agree on hand signals before backing up, including a signal that means stop.

questions.question: How should you use mirrors while driving?

options.text: Take quick glances at the mirrors.
Look in the mirrors for a long time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take quick glances at the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.
